Report every shortfall; never borrow another band. Freeze the unique evaluator worlds with build_unique_world_manifest (1 world per deterministic scenario, 3 per stochastic one). Check that every environment_world_digest is unique. In the library: compose_suite, freeze_composed_suite (suite directory + private suite-freeze.json) and schedule_composed_worlds, which also checks every scheduled world against the frozen calibrated world. Create one immutable EnvironmentPack (freeze_environment_pack) with a new suite ID, version and batch ID. Commit only digests publicly before evaluation: pack digest, suite hash, manifest hash, rule-set hash, counts per family x band x fire model. Seeds, key, scenarios and measurements stay in the private freeze record. Evaluate every model on the same pack, with its K, replay-verified. Record provider, model ID and version, date and K for every run. 15. Leakage and contamination No hidden material to developers. They get the public suite, the generator, the rules and the commitments. They never get hidden scenarios, seeds, world digests, bands or per-world results of a live suite. The observation contains no seed. No per-world results while a suite is live. Publish overall and per-family scores with intervals only. Provider and model identity are recorded per run (section 14, step 11). A suite is treated as exposed to every provider that served it. No hidden suite in release artifacts. Private material lives only under leak-guarded paths; tools/check_public_assets.py checks the built distribution; tests check that no study cache or generated suite is committed and that the tool and worlds.py contain no seed literal. Reveal only after retirement: generator seeds, selection key, pack and freeze record, so that anybody can check the suite with verify_regeneration. Canary policy. A canary string in prompts or archives can show, after the fact, that a copy of the material appeared somewhere it was searched for (a crawl, a dataset, a model output that reproduces it verbatim). It cannot show that a model was trained on the suite, and its absence proves nothing. EMBER observations are grid states, which a model can learn from without reproducing any string. This design therefore does not use a canary as a contamination test. A harness may add one to pack archives for provenance tracing only, and must describe it that way. Contamination check (when required). Before a round closes, if a model is suspected (for example a large jump between rounds), generate a fresh check suite with the same frozen rules, a new seed and a new key, and run that model and the calibration panel on it. A model whose paired score (against the panel) on the live suite exceeds its paired score on the check suite by more than the paired 95% interval is flagged for review. This is a statistical check of overfitting to the live suite, not proof of training contamination. 16. Refresh and version policy A live suite is replaced, never edited, and never replaced silently. Every replacement has a new suite ID and version, a new pack digest and a published reason. Scores on different suites are not pooled or ranked together. The scoring version is separate from the suite version: a suite records the scoring version it was calibrated with, and a scoring change does not rename a suite by itself. Trigger Action Leak of hidden material Retire at once; new suite; re-run affected models Contamination flag confirmed (section 15) Retire; new suite Saturation: the best model scores >= 90 overall or on Stress New calibration-panel version with a stronger reference; new suite Generator bug that affects selected worlds Retire; fix; new generator version; new suite Scoring or benchmark revision (SCORING_VERSION or rule change) Re-calibrate the bands on the new score; new suite Simulator or observation revision New suite (world digests change) Invalid hidden world (for example a wrong M* or a capacity artifact found later) Retire the suite and publish the defect; never drop a world from a live suite Scheduled New suite each evaluation round (at least every 6 months); retire and reveal the previous one To compare rounds, run the calibration panel on every suite and report models relative to it (a linking set), not raw scores across suites. 17. Final V1 proposal Item Value Primary families 10: single_exit_low_density (basic evacuation planning), single_exit_high_density (queue management at one exit), narrow_corridor_bottleneck (sequencing through a width-1 cut), split_flow_across_exits (load balancing across exits), crowd_100 (scale), maze_obstacle_routing (path finding with detours), deceptive_nearest_exit (exit choice by true route length), threatened_nearest_exit (fire anticipation), multiple_ignitions (several fire fronts), route_invalidation_replanning (replanning). central_ignition and multiple_exits_unequal_distance are secondary tags. Scenarios per family 16 Difficulty per family Easy 2, Moderate 4, Hard 6, Stress 4 Deterministic / stochastic per family 12 / 4 Unique fire trajectories per stochastic scenario 3 Total scenarios 160 Total unique worlds 240 (120 deterministic, 120 stochastic) Model trials K = 1 verified-deterministic; K = 3 otherwise Model episodes 240 (K = 1); 720 (K = 3) Expected 95% CI width about 7.9 points within a suite (about +-3.9); paired width between models at most about 5.8 points Candidate pool 4,000 candidates, then targeted top-up batches of 200 per short cell, cap 10,000 API calls per model about 5,800 (K = 1) or 17,500 (K = 3); worst case 22,000 or 66,000 Calibration panel version 1.0: nearest-exit-greedy, static-shortest-path, fire-aware-shortest-path, congestion-aware; random-legal as floor; privileged reference as bound only Admission and bands difficulty-calibration.md sections 4 to 6 World identity environment_world_digest (version 1.0); schedule build_unique_world_manifest Generation and freeze Section 14 (11 ordered steps) Refresh Section 16 Prerequisite Generator work in section 6 for a library-supported pipeline; until then evaluator-side tagging and rejection sampling

title: Difficulty calibration
description: Calibrating generated-world difficulty.
text: Difficulty bands and calibration (research, V1) Field Value Status Research design. Not merged. Uses the official EMBER Score (scoring version 1.0). Code Library since Phase 11: CALIBRATION_PANEL, measure_world, calibrate, difficulty_band, capacity_savable, capacity_ceiling, fire_evidence in emberbench.calibration (calibration panel 1.0, difficulty rules 1.0, admission rules 1.0); family_tags in emberbench.families; select_suite and the pool workflow in emberbench.composition. The research tool tools/analyze_suite_design.py imports them. See generator.md. Evidence suite-design-results.md (development pool: 1,120 generated scenarios, 2,320 unique worlds) Score used The official EMBER Score from emberbench.scoring (score_episode, score_evidence). The tool has no other score. This document defines how a scenario gets an admission decision and a difficulty band, and how the evaluator uses the bands to compose the unseen suite. The parent design is evaluation-suite-design.md. 1. Requirements A band is computed from measurements. Nobody labels a scenario by hand. The computation is deterministic and reproducible from the scenario, its unique worlds and the frozen calibration panel. No model under evaluation is an input. The rule is not fitted to any model. The rule is calibrated on development worlds (public development seeds) only. Hidden worlds are only measured, evaluator-side, with the rule frozen beforehand. The composed suite separates methods. It must not be mostly worlds where every reference policy scores about 100, or about 0. 2. The frozen calibration panel (version 1.0) Role Policy Use Panel member nearest-exit-greedy-v1 band input Panel member static-shortest-path-v1 band input Panel member fire-aware-shortest-path-v1 band input Panel member congestion-aware-v1 band input Floor reference random-legal-v1 reported only (the analogue of Procgen's R_min); it scores 0 on every public world Privileged reference M* (official max_evacuated), M_cap (section 6), official time and path bounds a bound only. It normalizes the official score and excludes capacity artifacts. It never sets a band. The panel is the four public, non-random V1 baselines, in the order of increasing information use. Its members, its version (CALIBRATION_PANEL_VERSION = "1.0") and the band thresholds are frozen and recorded in the freeze record of every suite. A change to any of them is a new panel version and needs new suites. No circular calibration. The panel is fixed before any model is evaluated. A model under evaluation is never a panel member and never an input to admission, banding or selection (tests check the signatures). The thresholds are fixed numbers with a stated meaning on the official score scale (section 4). They are not quantiles of a pool and not fitted to make any policy look good. The panel members define the bands, so their own scores on a selected suite are biased by the selection. The suite-design study therefore measures rank stability also with two comparators that are not panel members: a congestion-aware policy with an ε share of uniformly random legal actions, ε = 0.05 and ε = 0.2. fire-aware-shortest-path-v1 and congestion-aware-v1 are practically tied on the pool (mean 61.1 and 61.6). The design study does not count their order as evidence. 3. Evidence: structural proxies do not predict difficulty Rank correlation (Spearman) between each proxy and 100 - B over the admitted development scenarios, where B is the best panel score (section 4): Proxy rho population 0.35 crowd density 0.17 N / min cut 0.20 obstacle density -0.48 route redundancy 0.34 ignition-person distance -0.30 threatened share (privileged) 0.27 recoverable invalidation (privileged) 0.57 savable share M*/N (privileged) 0.04 No structural proxy reaches |rho| = 0.5. Obstacle density correlates negatively: mazes slow the fire and are easy for any planner. A Safety-Gym-style level ("more obstacles is harder") would be wrong here. The best single predictor is privileged: the share of savable people whose every static shortest route the fire cuts (0.57). It needs the seed, so it is evaluator-side. Proxies are therefore used for family tags and quality checks, not for bands. 4. Band definition For a scenario, take each panel member's mean official EMBER Score over the scenario's applicable unique worlds (worlds with M* > 0). B is the highest of the four means. Band Rule (official points) Best panel member, development pool (median avoidable losses) Easy B >= 80 0 Moderate 30 <= B < 80 1 Hard 10 <= B < 30 1.75 Stress B < 10 3 Why these cutpoints. The official score is steep in avoidable losses. With perfect quality, one avoidable loss gives at most 52.5 when M* = 10, 65.2 when M* = 20, 76.8 when M* = 100; two avoidable losses out of 10 give 28.8, three give 15.4 (computed with score_evidence). So: B >= 80 means that the best fair heuristic has no avoidable loss and a good quality. On the pool, the mean avoidable loss of the best member in the Easy band is 0.01. 30 <= B < 80 means about one avoidable loss (or none with a severe quality failure). 10 <= B < 30 means about two avoidable losses. B < 10 means three or more: the best V1 heuristic fails badly. This band is the headroom against saturation. The earlier proposal (before PR #32) used worst >= 90 and best >= 90 on a safety-only analysis score. On the official score, the old Easy rule worst >= 90 mostly selects saturated worlds (every panel member is at 95 or more on 28.6% of the pool worlds), which carry no ranking information. The rule is replaced by the B rule above and an explicit saturation exclusion (section 5). Why B, not the mean or the worst member. A band states how much of the attainable score the best fair V1 heuristic keeps: the regret of the strongest available reference, as in PAIRED (Dennis et al., 2020). The spread of the panel is used for admission (section 5), not for the band. 5. Admission rule (deterministic, in this order) Order Exclusion Rule Pool share 1 not_applicable no world has a savable person (M* = 0); the official score is NOT_APPLICABLE 0.9% 2 capacity_artifact mean capacity ceiling < 50 (section 6) 4.1% 3 saturated every panel member >= 95 24.1% 4 floor every panel member < 1 2.2% 5 no_separation panel spread B - worst < the official practical difference (1 point) 12.9% — admitted every other scenario; banded by B 55.7% A saturated or floor scenario carries no ranking information for V1-level policies. A no-separation scenario cannot rank the panel itself. All three still count in the pool statistics, so the acceptance rates of section 7 are honest. 6. Practical unsolvability: the capacity filter (M_cap) The official M* counts the people who can escape alone against the precomputed fire. It ignores that people share exits and cuts. In a dense single-exit room, M* can be 35 while at most 14 people can physically leave before the fire closes the exit. Every policy then "loses" 21 savable people, and the official score is 0 for every policy: the world measures the bound, not the policy. capacity_savable(scenario, seed) returns (M*, M_cap). M_cap <= M* adds the two capacity facts behind the official time bound Q_cut: at most one person leaves through an open exit cell per step; at most k_s people stand on the cut N(C) of a component C of the cells with wall distance > d at step s (the same cut groups as the official _cut_bound). Each savable person gets an interval of feasible steps per exit and per cut. The maximum number of people who fit is an interval scheduling problem, solved exactly by Glover's earliest-deadline greedy. M_cap is still an upper bound (the relaxation ignores movement conflicts), so it is safe to use as a filter. capacity_ceiling(N, M*, M_cap) is the best official score that a perfect policy can reach when M* - M_cap savable people are capacity-limited: score_evidence on synthetic evidence with M* - M_cap avoidable stranded people and perfect quality. It uses the official formula; the tool has no second implementation. Rule: a scenario whose mean capacity ceiling is below CEILING_MIN = 50 is excluded as a capacity artifact. The official score is not changed: M* stays the official reference. The filter only stops such scenarios from entering a suite. Measurement (development pool) Value applicable worlds with M_cap < M* 92 of 2,286 (4.0%) scenarios with such a world 75 scenarios excluded (ceiling < 50) 46 (41 of them would otherwise be Stress) panel runs that evacuated more than M_cap 0 (2,320 worlds x 4 members): the bound holds capacity-limited worlds where the best member reaches M_cap exactly 50: the bound is tight there public V1 suite M_cap = M* on all 73 unique worlds The artifacts come mostly from the dense-single recipe (34 of its 120 scenarios). Without the filter they would enter the Stress band, where every policy scores about 0 for a reason that no policy controls. 7. Calibration results on the development pool Mean official score of each comparator over the admitted units (scenarios with a final primary family) per band: Band Units nearest-exit-greedy static-shortest-path fire-aware-shortest-path congestion-aware noisy ε=0.05 noisy ε=0.2 Easy 264 14.2 76.6 93.0 94.0 85.7 49.9 Moderate 69 10.7 23.3 40.9 42.4 35.8 13.0 Hard 79 4.1 6.4 14.4 17.4 17.2 9.0 Stress 105 0.9 1.3 3.9 4.5 5.2 2.4 The bands are ordered for every comparator, including the two non-panel comparators. The calibration is not circular in effect either. The Easy band still separates policies strongly (nearest-exit-greedy 14.2 against congestion-aware 94.0): "Easy" means easy for an informed planner, not for every policy. The official score is bimodal on single scenarios (histogram of B: 224 of 1,110 applicable scenarios below 10, 595 at 90 or more). The Moderate band is the scarcest (7.9% of candidates). Public V1 suite, same rule (one world per deterministic scenario, 64 worlds for the stochastic one): pub-01 and pub-04 saturated; pub-03 and pub-08 Easy; pub-02 and pub-10 Moderate; pub-06, pub-07 and pub-09 Hard; pub-05 Stress. 8. Composition rule Every candidate gets its calibrate result and its family tags (family_tags, fixed thresholds on the structural profile and on the evaluator-side fire profile). select_suite(candidates, quotas, selection_key) fills the family x band quotas. Families are filled scarcest first; each candidate is used once and its selected family becomes its primary family; inside a cell the order is a keyed SHA-256 of the scenario content hash, so the private key, not the candidate order or a model, decides which candidate is taken. A cell that cannot be filled is reported as a shortfall. It is never filled from another band in silence. The evaluator generates more candidates for that cell (targeted recipe), or the freeze record states the shortfall. The fire-model quota (stochastic slots per family) is applied in the same way, as part of the cell key. Phase 11 implements this rule as emberbench.composition.select_suite (selection rules 1.0). Inside a family the bands are filled Easy..Stress and the stochastic cell of a band before its deterministic cell. The stochastic slots follow the PR #33 even-spread rule: Moderate 1, Hard 2, Stress 1 per family. Calibration and fire tags of a stochastic candidate are measured on exactly the 3 unique worlds that build_unique_world_manifest schedules for it. The targeted top-up of step 3 is compose_pool with the V1_TOP_UP recipe table (generator.md, section 5). 9. Known limits Bands are relative to V1 heuristics. A strong model can find Stress worlds solvable. That is the intended headroom; saturation triggers a new panel version (evaluation-suite-design.md, section 16). M_cap is a relaxation. Some admitted Stress worlds can still be harder than any policy can solve. The filter removes the clear capacity artifacts only. Family tags use fixed thresholds on measured properties. Since generator 1.1.0, describe_families uses the same rules (family rules 1.0) for its structural labels; the two fire-dependent families stay evaluator-side. The evaluator-side tags are the stratification key. The noisy comparators share their base policy with a panel member. They test rank stability; they are not independent agents. 10. Reproducibility and tests Every band and admission decision is a pure function of the scenario, its unique worlds (by environment_world_digest) and the frozen panel. The tool caches expensive runs outside the repository, keyed by every version; the reported numbers are recomputed from the final code. tests/test_suite_design.py checks the band thresholds, the admission order, the capacity bound on a scenario with M_cap < M*, Glover's greedy, the capacity ceiling against the official score, the official scoring of panel runs and the selector rules. tests/test_calibration.py checks the library rules, and tests/test_composition.py checks the composition pipeline.

title: Scenario schema
description: Scenario fields and validation rules.
text: Scenario schema, version 1.0 A scenario is one JSON object. All keys are required except description. Unknown keys are rejected at every level, so a typo cannot silently become a default. Numbers must be finite. Integers must be JSON integers (1, not 1.0 and not true). { "schema_version": "1.0", "scenario_id": "one_person_one_exit", "description": "optional free text", "grid": {"width": 7, "height": 3}, "obstacles": [[0, 0], [0, 1]], "exits": [{"id": "E1", "position": [1, 5]}], "people": [{"id": "P1", "position": [1, 1]}], "ignitions": [[1, 3]], "fire": {"model": "deterministic", "spread_interval": 1, "exits_flammable": true}, "movement": {"conflict_resolution": "lowest_id_wins", "enter_fire": "casualty"}, "termination": {"max_steps": 50}, "seed": 1 } Field Type Rules schema_version string Must be "1.0". scenario_id id Matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$. grid.width, grid.height int 1 to 1024. obstacles list of [row, col] In bounds, no duplicates. These are walls: impassable and non-flammable. exits list of {id, position} At least one. Unique IDs and positions. Not on an obstacle. people list of {id, position} At least one. Unique IDs and positions. Not on an obstacle, exit or ignition point. ignitions list of [row, col] Cells burning at step 0. May be empty. In bounds, no duplicates, not on an obstacle. On an exit only if fire.exits_flammable is true. fire.model "deterministic" | "stochastic" See the simulation contract. fire.spread_interval int ≥ 1 Fire spreads on steps where step % interval == 0. fire.exits_flammable bool Whether exits can catch fire and become unusable. fire.spread_probability number in [0, 1] Required for stochastic. Forbidden for deterministic. movement.conflict_resolution "lowest_id_wins" The only V1 rule. It is stated explicitly. movement.enter_fire "blocked" | "casualty" What happens when someone moves into a burning cell. termination.max_steps int, 1 to 100000 Step limit. seed int, 0 to 2^64 − 1 Default run seed. Simulator(scenario, seed=...) can override it, and the record stores the seed used. Evaluator-private: never shown to a model (see v1-fairness-spec.md). Canonical form and identity After parsing, the following lists are sorted: obstacles and ignitions by position, and exits and people by ID. Scenario.to_json() emits canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace). Scenario.content_hash() is its SHA-256. Input order therefore never changes a scenario's identity. Run records store the hash, so a replay against a different scenario is rejected. Fixtures tests/fixtures/scenarios/*.json are small test fixtures. Each description starts with TEST FIXTURE. and ends with an ASCII layout. They are not benchmark scoring scenarios, and they are not the hidden evaluation set. Fixture Purpose one_person_one_exit Basic movement and evacuation, no fire. blocked_shortest_route The shortest route crosses fire. The safe route is longer. Exits are not flammable. multiple_exits Three people, two exits, fire in the middle. narrow_corridor A one-wide queue, chain moves and exit throughput. fire_threatening_exit Fire burns the near exit at step 1. The far exit stays usable. stochastic_room Seeded stochastic spread with the blocked fire-entry policy. The canonical public V1 scenarios are a separate set in scenarios/public/v1/. See scenario-suite.md.

title: Versioning
description: Simulation, metric, scoring and package versions.
text: Versioning and release policy EMBERBench has three kinds of version. They answer different questions and change for different reasons. Never infer one from another. Kind Question it answers Where it lives Package version Which build of the Python distribution is installed? src/emberbench/_version.py (emberbench.__version__) Benchmark revision What does a score mean? Which scores may be compared? BENCHMARK_REVISION in src/emberbench/integrity.py Component contract versions Which exact rules or file format produced this artifact? One constant per component, listed below emberbench version --json reports all three: package_version, benchmark_revision and every component version (section 3). The output depends on no environment value. It reads the package version from the source, not from installed metadata. 1. Package version One source. src/emberbench/_version.py holds __version__. pyproject.toml reads it (dynamic = ["version"], [tool.setuptools.dynamic]), so the wheel and sdist metadata, the runtime attribute and the CLI cannot disagree. Do not write the version in any other file. Format. MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (Semantic Versioning 2.0.0), with an optional pre-release suffix (1.0.0rc1) that is also a valid PEP 440 version. Not in any benchmark artifact. No run record, manifest, result, statistics file, score report, environment pack, generated or composed suite or provenance record holds the package version. A package release alone therefore never changes a benchmark hash. The only registry entry that moves with it is cli.version-json, the bytes of emberbench version --json itself. Not the benchmark revision. The two are independent numbers. Package 0.1.0 implements benchmark revision 2. A benchmark revision never sets the package version, and a package release never sets the revision. Current decision. The package version stays 0.1.0. No version of EMBERBench has been tagged or published, so 0.1.0 is still the first release. Benchmark revision 2 is a pre-release revision: it replaced revision 1 before anything was released, and no published package or score used revision 1. Choosing a different first version (for example 1.0.0 for the V1 benchmark) is a maintainer decision at tag time; until one is recorded, the version stays 0.1.0. Changing it is a release step (see release-checklist.md), not part of feature work. Release rules Release Allowed changes Pinned hashes PATCH (x.y.Z) Bug fixes that change no artifact byte, documentation, packaging, CI and development tooling, performance work, clearer error messages. None may change. MINOR (x.Y.0) Backward-compatible additions: new library API, new CLI commands or options, new baselines under new IDs, new diagnostic artifacts, a tooling version bump that does not change what any score means (CLI_VERSION, BASELINES_VERSION, INTEGRITY_PROTOCOL_VERSION for a new optional record field, REPLAY_AUDIT_VERSION, ANIMATION_FORMAT_VERSION). Only the hashes owned by a bumped component, as listed in its changelog entry. MAJOR (X.0.0) A new BENCHMARK_REVISION after the first release, or an incompatible change to the public Python API or to CLI behaviour (removed command, changed exit code, changed artifact bytes of an existing command). Any, as listed in the changelog entry. While the package is below 1.0.0, a change that needs a MAJOR release increments MINOR instead (0.Y.0), as Semantic Versioning allows for 0.y.z. A change that would need a MAJOR (or pre-1.0 MINOR) release but is not ready for one waits. Do not ship it in a smaller release. 2. Benchmark revision BENCHMARK_REVISION = "2" is the V1 benchmark. The revision defines what a score means. Scores and provenance from different revisions are never compared, and provenance of another revision fails verification (integrity.md, section 12). Revision 2 is one pre-release step from revision 1. It takes in the official EMBER Score (SCORING_VERSION 1.0), environment packs and unique-world identity (ENVIRONMENT_PACK_VERSION, ENVIRONMENT_WORLD_VERSION), generator 1.1 (GENERATOR_VERSION 1.1.0, config and generation manifest 1.1) and the suite-definition contracts (family rules, calibration panel, difficulty and admission rules, composition, selection, recipe catalog, suite freeze record). Revision 1 was never released. A new benchmark revision is mandatory for: a change to any version that benchmark_versions() returns (the "In provenance" column of section 3). The full list, with the reason for each, is in integrity.md, section 12; a change to the content of the canonical public suite that scored comparisons use (a new suite_version); discovered held-out leakage that the current protocol permits, or any other flaw in the evaluation protocol; a material bug that affects ranking or comparison, even when the fix is small. A new revision is not needed for: package-only changes, documentation, CLI presentation, new or changed reference baselines (they are not scored submissions; bump BASELINES_VERSION), replay and audit tooling that does not change what verify_record accepts, and a regenerated held-out batch under the same code (see integrity.md, section 12). 3. Component contract versions Each component owns one version. Its document gives the exact bump rule. "In provenance" is yes exactly for the versions that benchmark_versions() returns: evaluation provenance records them and verify_evaluation_provenance fails closed on any difference. A change to one of them needs a new BENCHMARK_REVISION (section 2). The other versions are tooling contracts: they never change what a score means. Constant Value In provenance Owner Owned hashes and artifacts BENCHMARK_REVISION 2 yes src/emberbench/integrity.py, integrity.md Meaning of every score SIMULATOR_VERSION 0.2.0 yes src/emberbench/__init__.py, simulation-contract.md Run record bytes and digests, golden trajectories, stochastic golden traces OBSERVATION_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/observation.py, v1-fairness-spec.md Run record header, model input ACTION_SCHEMA_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/agent.py, model-interface.md Model output format SCHEMA_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/scenario.py, scenario-schema.md Scenario content hashes METRICS_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/metrics.py, metrics.md Episode metrics CROWD_DIAGNOSTICS_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/crowd.py, crowd-diagnostics.md Crowd diagnostic digests STATISTICS_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/statistics.py, statistics.md Aggregate and paired statistics digests GENERATOR_VERSION 1.1.0 yes src/emberbench/generator.py, procedural-generation.md Generated scenarios, generation and generated suite hashes GENERATOR_CONFIG_VERSION 1.1 yes src/emberbench/generator.py Generator config hash GENERATION_MANIFEST_VERSION 1.1 yes src/emberbench/generator.py generation.json format and generation hash EVALUATION_MANIFEST_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/evaluation.py, evaluation.md Evaluation manifest hash and file bytes EVALUATION_RESULT_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/evaluation.py, evaluation.md Evaluation result files SCORING_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/scoring.py, scoring.md Scoring constants digest, episode scores, score report digests ENVIRONMENT_PACK_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/environment_pack.py, environment-pack.md pack.json and the pack digest ENVIRONMENT_WORLD_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/worlds.py, evaluation-suite-design.md Environment world digests (unique-world identity) FAMILY_RULES_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/families.py, generator.md Family rule record, family tags CALIBRATION_PANEL_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/calibration.py, difficulty-calibration.md Calibration rule record (panel) DIFFICULTY_RULES_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/calibration.py, difficulty-calibration.md Calibration rule record (bands) ADMISSION_RULES_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/calibration.py, difficulty-calibration.md Calibration rule record (admission) COMPOSITION_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/composition.py, generator.md Composition rule set digest SELECTION_RULES_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/composition.py, generator.md Composition rule set digest (selection) RECIPE_CATALOG_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/composition.py, generator.md Composition rule set digest (recipes) SUITE_FREEZE_RECORD_VERSION 1.0 yes src/emberbench/composition.py, generator.md Suite freeze record format CLI_VERSION 1.0 no src/emberbench/cli.py, cli.md Command tree, exit codes, JSON output keys, CLI artifact bytes BASELINES_VERSION 1.0 no src/emberbench/baselines.py, baselines.md Baseline config and result digests INTEGRITY_PROTOCOL_VERSION 1.0 no src/emberbench/integrity.py, integrity.md Provenance record format and digests REPLAY_AUDIT_VERSION 1.0 no src/emberbench/audit.py, replay-visualization.md Replay audit digests ANIMATION_FORMAT_VERSION 1.0 no src/emberbench/visualization.py, replay-visualization.md Animation JSON digests GENERATED_SUITE_VERSION 1.0.0 no src/emberbench/generator.py suite_version label of every generated suite manifest; content identity is the generated suite hash, owned by GENERATOR_VERSION. Not reported separately COMPOSED_SUITE_VERSION 1.0.0 no src/emberbench/composition.py suite_version label of every composed suite manifest; content identity is owned by the composition versions. Not reported separately The public suite has its own suite_version (1.0.0) in scenarios/public/v1/manifest.json. A released suite is never edited; a changed suite is a new suite version (scenario-suite.md). Rules for every component version: Bump by hand, on purpose. No tool, script or CI step bumps a component version. A failing pinned-hash test is the signal; the fix is a deliberate bump in the same change, never an edited pin alone. Bump only the owner. A change in one component does not bump the others. A package release does not bump any component. Report it. Every component version appears in emberbench version --json (except the two suite_version labels, see the table) and in the table above. The benchmark-defining part of emberbench version is built from benchmark_versions(), so a version that provenance pins is reported by construction. Record it. The changelog entry names every bumped component, its old and new value, and every pinned hash that changed. tests/test_release.py enforces this. It imports every emberbench module and collects each *_VERSION string constant and BENCHMARK_REVISION. It fails when one of them is missing from emberbench version (unless it is a listed suite_version label), from the table above (with the right "In provenance" value), from the changelog, or from the release checklist, and when a benchmark_versions() entry has no owning constant. 4. When pinned hashes may change The pinned hashes are listed in the regression digest registry (tests/fixtures/release/digest_registry.json, see release-checklist.md). A pinned hash may change only when all of these hold: the component that owns it (table above, and the owner field of the registry entry) has a new version in the same change; the change is not a PATCH release; the registry entry, the test pin that it mirrors and the changelog are updated together, and the changelog says why; if the change alters what a score means, BENCHMARK_REVISION is bumped too (section 2). Platform, Python version (within requires-python), PYTHONHASHSEED, locale, time zone, working directory, path spelling and line endings of accepted inputs never change a pinned hash. If one of them does, that is a bug. The one deliberate exception is an environment pack: it freezes the exact bytes of its files (environment-pack.md), so its digest, and a score report that names it, follow the file bytes. The repository's .gitattributes keeps those files LF on every platform. 5. Components added in parallel work A branch that adds a component with its own version (for example a new artifact format) must, before it merges or when release work syncs with it: add the constant to the table in section 3 and, if it defines what a score means, to benchmark_versions() (then emberbench version reports it automatically); otherwise add it to the tooling part of version_info() in src/emberbench/cli.py; add it to the version review in release-checklist.md; add its frozen digests to the registry; add a changelog entry.

title: Replay audit tools
description: Command-line replay audit and visualization documentation.
text: Replay audit and visualization (replay audit version 1.0, animation format version 1.0) This document defines the read-only replay audit and the two views built from it: canonical text frames and a portable JSON animation export. emberbench.build_replay_audit(scenario, record, *, crowd=False) -> ReplayAudit is in src/emberbench/audit.py. render_frame, build_animation, animation_json, export_animation and verify_animation are in src/emberbench/visualization.py. The tests are in tests/test_replay_audit.py. Visualization never affects benchmark results. The audit and every view only read an authenticated RunRecord. They do not run the simulator rules again, they do not change a record, and no metric, statistic, baseline, integrity check or CLI command reads them. 1. Read-only guarantee Authenticated input only. build_replay_audit first calls validate_run_record, the same three stages that the metrics, the crowd diagnostics and emberbench replay verify use: version and scenario binding, structural invariants, and a full simulator replay that must reproduce the record byte for byte. Any failure raises ReplayAuditError (a subclass of MetricsInputError). There is no function that audits or renders an unchecked record. Complete episodes only. As for the metrics, the record must reach termination. A replayable prefix is rejected. The shortest valid episode has one step. No inference. Every event in the audit is an event in the record. Every count is a count of recorded values. There is no fire prediction, no path planning and no re-simulation of a trajectory. No score. The congestion overlay copies raw counts. There is no crowd score and no ratio. No environment. The artifacts hold no timestamps, no file paths, no host or user names and no interpreter details. verify_replay_audit(scenario, record, audit) and verify_animation(scenario, record, animation) rebuild the artifact from the authenticated record and require byte-identical canonical JSON. They fail closed on a wrong scenario, a wrong hash, an incompatible version, a structurally invalid record, a replay mismatch, or an edited artifact. 2. Audit model ReplayAudit.to_dict() has exactly these keys: Key Meaning replay_audit_version "1.0" (REPLAY_AUDIT_VERSION) simulator_version, observation_version, schema_version copied from the record header scenario_id, scenario_hash, seed copied from the record header record_digest RunRecord.digest() of the audited record map width, height, walls (row-major), exits ({id, position}, exit-ID order) episode_steps number of recorded steps N termination_reason all_resolved or max_steps timeline N + 1 frames, see section 3 people one path per person, person-ID order, see section 4 fire initial_burning and N fire deltas, see section 5 crowd the congestion overlay, or null unless crowd=True, see section 6 Cells are [row, col] lists. ReplayAudit.to_json() is canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, ASCII). ReplayAudit.digest() is its SHA-256. 3. Timeline and frame semantics Frame k describes the state after step k. Frame 0 is the initial state. audit.frame(k) returns frame k for 0 <= k <= N; other values raise ValueError (or TypeError for a non-integer). Lookup is constant time: audit.timeline[k].step == k. Field Frame 0 Frame k >= 1 movements [] the recorded MoveResolution of every person active at decision time: person_id, action (the attempted action), origin, target, final, outcome newly_ignited [] StepRecord.ignited evacuations [] StepRecord.evacuations (person_id, exit_id, position) casualties [] StepRecord.casualties (person_id, position, cause) people every person after the step: id, position, status same burning_count number of burning cells same active_count active people same evacuated_total, casualty_total cumulative, up to and including the step same trapped the recorded trapped diagnostic, sorted same terminated, termination_reason false, null set only on frame N A resolved person keeps the last cell occupied (the exit, or the burning cell), as in SimState. 4. Person paths audit.person(person_id) returns a PersonPath: Field Meaning initial_position position at step 0 steps one entry for each step in which the person was active at decision time: step, action, outcome, origin, target, position (the cell after movement). Steps run from 1 to len(steps) with no gaps. final_status evacuated, casualty, or active final_position the person's position in the final state resolution_step the evacuation or casualty step; null if unresolved exit_id the exit used; set only for an evacuation casualty_cause entered_fire or fire_spread; set only for a casualty trapped_at_end true only for an unresolved person in the final trapped set final_status == "active" means unresolved: the episode ended at max_steps with the person still on the grid. PersonPath.unresolved is the same test. For a resolved person the last entry of steps is the resolution step. PersonPath.position_at(k) returns the position after step k, read from the path. The tests check that it equals SimState.person(id).position for every person and every step, and that each path entry equals the person's recorded MoveResolution. The paths come from one pass over the recorded movements; nothing is simulated again. 5. Fire timeline fire.initial_burning is the burning set at step 0 (the scenario ignitions). fire.steps[k - 1] (or audit.fire_delta(k)) is the delta for step k: Field Meaning burning_before cells burning before step k (the state after step k - 1) newly_ignited cells ignited in step k (StepRecord.ignited) burning_after cells burning after step k (StepRecord.state.burning) Every delta satisfies burning_after == burning_before | newly_ignited, and burning_before and newly_ignited are disjoint. audit.burning_at(k) returns the burning set after step k. Stochastic fire is audited the same way: the deltas are the recorded ignitions of that seed. There is no delta after step N and no prediction. All cell lists are in row-major order. 6. Congestion overlay build_replay_audit(..., crowd=True) calls compute_crowd_diagnostics on the same inputs and attaches an overlay. It uses the definitions in crowd-diagnostics.md. It does not define a second notion of congestion. The overlay is optional, and it never changes any other audit field. Field Meaning crowd_diagnostics_version the crowd diagnostics version crowd_diagnostics_digest CrowdDiagnostics.digest() of the diagnostics used steps[k - 1].blocked every recorded blocked move of step k: person_id, origin, target, reason (the recorded blocked_* outcome) steps[k - 1].contested_cells target cells with two or more contenders in step k, row-major; each lists the contenders in person-ID order with their recorded outcome steps[k - 1].congestion_blocks blocked_occupied + blocked_conflict + blocked_cycle in step k steps[k - 1].evacuations_by_exit evacuations per exit in step k hotspots the CellCongestion entries with at least one congestion block, row-major exit_throughput CrowdDiagnostics.exits (ExitLoadSignals) A contender is a movement attempt that passed the static boundary, wall and fire checks (the crowd diagnostics definition). The overlay build checks that the number of blocked moves, contested cells, the largest contender group and the congestion blocks of every step equal the matching StepCrowdSignals values. A difference raises ReplayAuditError. 7. Canonical text renderer render_frame(audit, step, *, events=False, header=False) returns one ASCII frame. Rows are joined with \n. There is no trailing newline and no colour. render_initial(audit) is frame 0 and render_final(audit) is frame N. Legend The legend is in precedence order. When several entries apply to one cell, the first one wins. Glyph Meaning Layer # wall base X casualty in this step event V evacuation in this step event f newly ignited in this step event F burning cell base P active person base E exit that is not burning base . empty cell base Event glyphs appear only with events=True. Frame 0 has no events. Without events, a frame equals emberbench.render(scenario, state) for the same state. The tests check this for every step of every audited episode. A burning exit shows F. A casualty cell is always burning, so it shows F, or X in the casualty step with events. With header=True the first line is step k/N active=a evacuated=e casualties=c burning=b, followed by terminated=<reason> on the final frame. colorize(text) adds ANSI colour for a human terminal. Its output is never canonical and never enters an artifact. Example: one person enters a fire cell while another evacuates, and the fire spreads in the same step (#PF.PE# at step 0): step 1/1 active=0 evacuated=1 casualties=1 burning=3 terminated=all_resolved ####### #fXf.V# ####### 8. Portable animation schema build_animation(audit) returns a provider-neutral document. It holds data only: no HTML, no script, no styling. animation_json(audit) is its canonical JSON, and export_animation(scenario, record, *, crowd=False) authenticates, audits and serialises in one call. Top-level keys: Key Meaning animation_format_version "1.0" (ANIMATION_FORMAT_VERSION), separate from the audit version replay_audit_version the audit version the document was built from source simulator_version, observation_version, schema_version, scenario_id, scenario_hash, seed, record_digest, audit_digest map as in the audit people every person ID, sorted episode_steps, termination_reason as in the audit frames N + 1 frames, step order congestion null, or hotspots and exit_throughput from the overlay Each frame has these keys: Key Meaning step 0..N people every person: id, position, status (person-ID order) burning every burning cell after the step (row-major) newly_ignited cells ignited in the step movements movement events: person_id, action, origin, target, final, outcome evacuations evacuation events casualties casualty events congestion null without the overlay; otherwise blocked and contested_cells for the step (empty at step 0) terminated, termination_reason as in the timeline A viewer can draw any frame from map and one frame alone. 9. Determinism The same record gives byte-identical audit JSON, animation JSON and text frames, also after a RunRecord JSON round trip. People are in person-ID order, cells in row-major order, exits in exit-ID order and events in the recorded (person-ID) order. The tests pin golden digests of the audit, the animation and the text frames, and check them in subprocesses with PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1 and 10. Cost The audit is built in one pass over the steps. Its size is linear in the record: frames hold every person, and fire deltas hold the burning sets before and after each step. The tests audit a 100-person crowd run and a long stochastic run. There is no wall-clock gate. 11. Versions REPLAY_AUDIT_VERSION and ANIMATION_FORMAT_VERSION change only when a field of these artifacts changes. This feature changes no simulator, observation, action schema, scenario schema, metric, statistic, generator, baseline, integrity protocol or CLI version, and no suite hash.

title: Release checklist
description: Protocol and release validation requirements.
text: Release checklist Follow every step for every release. A release is an annotated git tag and, optionally, a published wheel and sdist. The version policy is in versioning.md. Never publish from a branch, a dirty tree or a local build that did not pass section 3. Commands are for a POSIX shell (Linux or macOS). On Windows use .venv\Scripts\activate instead of . .venv/bin/activate; the other commands are the same. 1. Release blockers Each of these must be resolved before a tag: License. The maintainers selected the Apache License 2.0 (Apache-2.0). The release needs all of: 1. the canonical Apache License 2.0 text as LICENSE at the repository root; 2. in pyproject.toml, [project]: license = "Apache-2.0" and license-files = ["LICENSE"]; 3. the license name in this checklist and in the changelog entry. python tools/check_release.py ... --require-license fails if one is missing, or if the wheel lacks License-Expression, License-File or the LICENSE file. A license change is a maintainer decision; no tool or pull request makes it. Pending V1 pull requests. Every pull request accepted for V1 is merged, main contains it, and this checklist runs on that main. Package version decision. The package version stays 0.1.0 unless the maintainers record another first release version (versioning.md, section 1). 2. Clean checkout and pinned tools git clone https://github.com/Aryabhatta-0/EMBERBench.git emberbench-release cd emberbench-release git checkout main git status --porcelain git status --porcelain prints nothing. Record the commit: git rev-parse HEAD. python -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -c tools/dev-constraints.txt pip python -m pip install -c tools/dev-constraints.txt -e ".[dev]" python tools/check_dev_constraints.py --installed The last command reports 0 problem(s): every installed tool and every dependency of a tool is the pinned version. 3. Release gates All CI is green on the exact commit: the six test jobs (Ubuntu, Windows and macOS on Python 3.12 and 3.13) and the packaging job. Then, locally: python -m mypy --strict python -m pytest -q EMBERBENCH_RELEASE_SMOKE=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_release.py python tests/release_digests.py --check python tools/check_release.py --contracts-only python tools/check_public_assets.py --untracked Also run the full opt-in mode of the public development evaluation pack (tests/test_evaluation_pack.py, PR #31). It reproduces the golden index and REPORT.md: EMBERBENCH_FULL_PACK=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_evaluation_pack.py Then build, check and install the release archives with the pinned build backend, offline: python -m pip download -c tools/dev-constraints.txt --no-deps --only-binary=:all: --dest wheelhouse setuptools SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct) python tools/check_release.py --dist dist --wheelhouse wheelhouse --require-license --require-clean tools/check_release.py prints each step and fails closed with the reason. All of these must hold: strict mypy reports no issues and the full test suite passes, including the opt-in release smoke; tests/release_digests.py --check prints registry verified; the leak guard reports 0 violations for the repository, the wheel and the sdist. No held-out material (hidden suite, private evaluation manifest, private suite freeze record, selection keys, private seeds, submission metadata, evaluator workspaces, caches) is in the repository, the wheel or the sdist. Never widen the leak-guard allowlist to make a release pass; tools/check_release.py passes: the version contracts match the docs, two clean builds give byte-identical wheels, the wheel built from the sdist equals the wheel built from the tree, the wheel builds offline from the sdist with only the pinned build backend, the metadata and the license are present, the wheel holds only package code, the wheel installs into a clean virtual environment under a path with spaces and runs from there, the registry recomputes with the installed wheel, and the leak guard passes. Install the checked wheel once more by hand and look at its version output: python -m venv "release smoke" "release smoke/bin/python" -m pip install --no-index --no-deps dist/emberbench-*.whl "release smoke/bin/emberbench" version --json "release smoke/bin/python" -I -m emberbench version --json Both print the same JSON with the package version and benchmark revision of this release. 4. Version and hash review Compare with the previous release tag (<previous-tag>; skip the diffs for the first release). Benchmark-defining versions. Each of these is pinned by provenance; a change to any of them needs a new BENCHMARK_REVISION (versioning.md, section 2): BENCHMARK_REVISION, SIMULATOR_VERSION, OBSERVATION_VERSION, ACTION_SCHEMA_VERSION, SCHEMA_VERSION, METRICS_VERSION, CROWD_DIAGNOSTICS_VERSION, STATISTICS_VERSION, GENERATOR_VERSION, GENERATOR_CONFIG_VERSION, GENERATION_MANIFEST_VERSION, EVALUATION_MANIFEST_VERSION, EVALUATION_RESULT_VERSION, SCORING_VERSION, ENVIRONMENT_PACK_VERSION, ENVIRONMENT_WORLD_VERSION, FAMILY_RULES_VERSION, CALIBRATION_PANEL_VERSION, DIFFICULTY_RULES_VERSION, ADMISSION_RULES_VERSION, COMPOSITION_VERSION, SELECTION_RULES_VERSION, RECIPE_CATALOG_VERSION, SUITE_FREEZE_RECORD_VERSION. Tooling versions. A change needs at least a MINOR release: CLI_VERSION, BASELINES_VERSION, INTEGRITY_PROTOCOL_VERSION, REPLAY_AUDIT_VERSION, ANIMATION_FORMAT_VERSION. Suite labels: GENERATED_SUITE_VERSION, COMPOSED_SUITE_VERSION. Every changed version has a reason in the changelog, no version moved without an intended change, and no intended change is missing a bump: git diff <previous-tag> -- src/emberbench docs/versioning.md Frozen hashes reviewed. Every changed registry entry has a bumped owner version and a changelog line. For a PATCH release the file has not changed: git diff <previous-tag> -- tests/fixtures/release/digest_registry.json The package version in src/emberbench/_version.py (the only place) follows versioning.md, section 1. A package version change also changes the registry entry cli.version-json.stdout_sha256 and nothing else; regenerate it with python tests/release_digests.py --write and review the diff. The changelog (changelog.md) is updated: rename "Unreleased" to the version, add the release date, and list the package version, benchmark revision, changed component versions and changed hashes. tools/check_release.py fails on a changelog that does not name the current versions. Public docs are updated: README status, every document of a changed component, cli.md for CLI changes. No document states a stale benchmark revision (tools/check_release.py checks this). 5. Tag and publish Only after sections 1 to 4, on the checked commit: git tag -a v<version> -m "EMBERBench <version> (benchmark revision <revision>)" git push origin v<version> Publish exactly the wheel and sdist that tools/check_release.py wrote to dist/ for that commit. Do not rebuild for publishing. Create the release notes from the changelog entry and attach dist/*. 6. Rollback and revision: a benchmark bug found after a release There is no rollback in place. Never move or delete a published tag, and never replace a published file. Users who need the previous behaviour pin the previous release; the fix goes forward as a new release. Triage. Decide if the bug changes any run record, metric, statistic, generated scenario, environment pack, world identity, score or provenance for some input. It does not (crash, wrong message, packaging, docs): fix it and release a PATCH version. No pinned hash may change. It does, or it can change a ranking or comparison: it is a benchmark bug. Continue below. Announce the bug with the affected releases, components and benchmark revision. Mark the results of the affected revision as affected; do not delete them. Fix it with a bump of the owning component version and of BENCHMARK_REVISION, updated pins and registry entries, and a changelog entry that names the bug. Release a new MAJOR version (MINOR while the package is below 1.0.0). Re-evaluate every model to compare on the new revision. Scores of different revisions are never compared or merged. If the bug exposed held-out material, also follow integrity.md, section 12: retire the batch, keep its provenance and mark its results as compromised. To withdraw a broken package (not a benchmark bug), yank it on the package index and release a fixed PATCH version. Reproducibility boundary What tools/check_release.py tests, on the CI packaging job (Ubuntu, Python 3.12, the pinned tools) and locally: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is frozen: the value of the environment variable, or the commit time of HEAD when it is unset. Every wheel member carries that time. Two builds from two clean copies of the same commit, with the same SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and the same pinned tools, give byte-identical wheels. Their sdists have identical member names and member contents. The sdist archives are not byte-identical: the gzip header and the tar member times come from the build. Only the normalized comparison is required. The wheel built from the sdist, the wheel built from the source tree and the wheel built offline from the sdist in an isolated environment with only the pinned setuptools have identical members and contents. The claim is exactly: the same source commit, the same SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and the same pinned toolchain produce byte-identical wheels. Not claimed: byte-identical archives across operating systems, Python versions or tool versions, or across different SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH values. The benchmark artifacts themselves (records, manifests, results, statistics, scores, packs, generated suites, provenance) are byte-identical on every supported platform; the registry and the golden tests check that in all six CI jobs. Regression digest registry tests/fixtures/release/digest_registry.json holds one digest per release-visible contract. SPEC in tests/release_digests.py is its source: each entry names its owner version, the test pin it mirrors and what it covers. Every value is recomputed from public development assets and test fixtures; no entry holds a path, a timestamp, a host value, a private seed or held-out material. python tests/release_digests.py --check recomputes it and prints a registry/computed diff on drift. tests/test_release.py compares it with the test pins it mirrors and recomputes it in fresh interpreters under other hash seeds, locales, time zones, I/O encodings, a working directory with spaces and a CRLF copy of the public suite. Under the CRLF copy only the environment pack digest and the score report that names it change, because a pack pins exact file bytes by design (versioning.md, section 4). tools/check_release.py recomputes it with the installed wheel. python tests/release_digests.py --write regenerates it. Use it only for a deliberate change with a bumped owner version and a changelog entry (versioning.md, section 4). Development tool constraints pyproject.toml declares bounded ranges for the development and build tools. tools/dev-constraints.txt pins the exact version of every tool and transitive dependency, and CI installs only those versions (PIP_CONSTRAINT, PIP_BUILD_CONSTRAINT). A new upstream release therefore cannot change CI until someone refreshes the pins in a pull request. Runtime dependencies stay empty. To refresh the pins: If a tool needs a new major version, widen its range in pyproject.toml first and review its release notes. Run python tools/refresh_dev_constraints.py --write (network access needed). It resolves the ranges for every CI platform and Python version and fails if they disagree. Run the release gates in section 3. Fix new strict mypy findings in the same pull request. Open a pull request that changes only the pins (and the ranges, if needed). CI fails on any unpinned or drifted installed tool or dependency of a tool (tools/check_dev_constraints.py --installed follows the declared tools' Requires-Dist under each platform's markers; packages a hosted runner preinstalls for itself are not checked); add a reported platform-only pin by hand.

title: Changelog
description: Recorded benchmark changes.
text: Changelog Notable changes to EMBERBench. The version policy is in versioning.md. Each release entry names the package version, the benchmark revision, every component version that changed and every pinned hash that changed. Entries reference the pull requests in Aryabhatta-0/EMBERBench that introduced each part. Dates are added only when a release is tagged. Unreleased: V1 (package 0.1.0, benchmark revision 2) No version of EMBERBench has been released yet. This entry collects the V1 milestones that are in main. Release them by following release-checklist.md. The package version stays 0.1.0 until the maintainers record a different first release version (versioning.md, section 1). License: Apache License 2.0 (Apache-2.0), selected by the maintainers: LICENSE at the repository root, and license = "Apache-2.0" with license-files = ["LICENSE"] in pyproject.toml, so the wheel and sdist carry License-Expression, License-File and the license text. Benchmark-defining versions (all pinned by evaluation provenance through benchmark_versions()): SIMULATOR_VERSION 0.2.0, OBSERVATION_VERSION 1.0, ACTION_SCHEMA_VERSION 1.0, SCHEMA_VERSION 1.0, METRICS_VERSION 1.0, CROWD_DIAGNOSTICS_VERSION 1.0, STATISTICS_VERSION 1.0, GENERATOR_VERSION 1.1.0, GENERATOR_CONFIG_VERSION 1.1, GENERATION_MANIFEST_VERSION 1.1, EVALUATION_MANIFEST_VERSION 1.0, EVALUATION_RESULT_VERSION 1.0, SCORING_VERSION 1.0, ENVIRONMENT_PACK_VERSION 1.0, ENVIRONMENT_WORLD_VERSION 1.0, FAMILY_RULES_VERSION 1.0, CALIBRATION_PANEL_VERSION 1.0, DIFFICULTY_RULES_VERSION 1.0, ADMISSION_RULES_VERSION 1.0, COMPOSITION_VERSION 1.0, SELECTION_RULES_VERSION 1.0, RECIPE_CATALOG_VERSION 1.0, SUITE_FREEZE_RECORD_VERSION 1.0. Tooling versions: CLI_VERSION 1.0, BASELINES_VERSION 1.0, INTEGRITY_PROTOCOL_VERSION 1.0, REPLAY_AUDIT_VERSION 1.0, ANIMATION_FORMAT_VERSION 1.0. Suite labels: GENERATED_SUITE_VERSION 1.0.0, COMPOSED_SUITE_VERSION 1.0.0. Public suite suite_version 1.0.0. Milestones Deterministic simulator (Phase 1, PR #2): benchmark contract, grid scenarios, the deterministic simulator, run records with digests, and replay. Fairness contract (Phase 2, PR #17): the frozen V1 fairness and semantics specification (v1-fairness-spec.md). SIMULATOR_VERSION went from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0: the run record header gained observation_version; the dynamics did not change. Metrics (Phase 3, PR #18): auditable per-episode metrics (metrics.md). Fixed public suite (Phase 4, PR #19): the canonical V1 public scenario suite with pinned hashes (scenario-suite.md). It is a public development and diagnostic suite, not the hidden scored suite. Paired evaluation (Phase 5, PR #20): exact scenario + seed manifests and resumable, paired evaluation runs (evaluation.md). Stochastic hazard (Phase 6, PR #21): the matched V1 stochastic fire contract with cross-platform golden traces (simulation-contract.md). Crowd diagnostics (Phase 7, PR #22): queue and throughput diagnostics (crowd-diagnostics.md). Observation/action contract (Phase 7, PR #23): the provider-independent agent, observation and action contract (model-interface.md). Statistics (Phase 8, PR #24): deterministic aggregate and paired statistics (statistics.md). Generator (Phase 8, PR #25): the procedural unseen scenario generator (procedural-generation.md). Integrity and provenance (Phase 9, PR #26, issue #14): the fail-closed hidden-test integrity protocol, provenance records and the public-asset leak guard (integrity.md). Baselines (Phase 9, PR #27): deterministic reference baseline agents (baselines.md). CLI (Phase 9, PR #28): the reproducible, provider-free emberbench command (cli.md). Replay and visualization (Phase 10, PR #29): read-only replay audit, ASCII frames and the JSON animation export (REPLAY_AUDIT_VERSION 1.0, ANIMATION_FORMAT_VERSION 1.0; replay-visualization.md). Official EMBER Score and EnvironmentPack (Phase 10, PR #32): scoring 1.0 with person-level loss attribution and severe quality gates, frozen environment packs that pin scenario bytes, schedule, versions and fire worlds (scoring.md, environment-pack.md). Coordination is not a score component: it was removed before scoring 1.0 was frozen (benchmark-methodology.md, section 5.12). Scientific suite design and unique-world identity (PR #33): environment_world_digest and build_unique_world_manifest, so a deterministic scenario is evaluated once instead of once per seed (evaluation-suite-design.md). Generator 1.1 and 10-family coverage (Phase 11, PR #34): generator 1.1.0 (config and generation manifest 1.1), the ten V1 family rules, calibration panel, difficulty and admission rules, composition, selection, recipe catalog and suite freeze record (generator.md, difficulty-calibration.md). Benchmark revision 2 (PR #34): BENCHMARK_REVISION went from 1 to 2 before any release, and benchmark_versions() pins every benchmark-defining version above. Revision 1 was never released. Public development evaluation pack (research lane, PR #31): the official EMBER Score of the fair reference agents on the 19 unique worlds of the public suite, one frozen environment pack, fail-closed resume and --verify, and the golden index and REPORT.md (tools/experiments/v1/README.md). It is not a hidden-suite leaderboard and changes no version or pinned hash. Remote-model runner (research lane): any model behind a base URL and an API key (OpenAI-compatible chat, Anthropic Messages or the Jev/SubQ decision API) on the same environment pack, with the same official scoring and paired comparisons against the reference runs (tools/experiments/remote/README.md). It changes no version or pinned hash. Results website: moved to its own repository, Aryabhatta-0/EMBERBench-site. It builds its data from the official score reports of EMBERBench runs, with the emberbench package pinned to a commit of this repository. The first version (docs/site, tools/build_results_site.py and .github/workflows/pages.yml, PR #36) is removed from this repository. Release hardening (Phase 10, issue #16, PR #30) One authoritative package version in src/emberbench/_version.py, exposed as emberbench.__version__ and as package_version in emberbench version. emberbench version --json reports every version of benchmark_versions() by construction, plus the tooling versions. No component version changed. Version and release policy (versioning.md) and release checklist (release-checklist.md). Development tooling pinned by tools/dev-constraints.txt, with bounded ranges in pyproject.toml. tools/check_release.py: version-contract and docs consistency, two clean builds compared, wheel built from the sdist offline, wheel content and size limits, clean-venv install, registry recomputed with the installed wheel, leak guard, and the license blocker. Regression digest registry (tests/fixtures/release/digest_registry.json, 31 entries) rebuilt for the V1 contracts; it adds scoring, environment pack, environment world, rule set, replay, version and CLI pins. The generator and provenance entries changed with generator 1.1 and revision 2 (PR #34); no pinned hash changed in this PR.
